subject: Turn an inspection report into a property-specific scope
preheader: Prioritize safety, systems, moisture, structure, and written local estimates

marketSnapshot.headline: The report starts due diligence; it does not price the work
marketSnapshot.body: Inspection findings vary in severity, scope, code impact, insurability, and cost. Group the findings, identify which require specialist review, and obtain local written estimates before changing an acquisition model or negotiating. Do not convert a generic online cost band into a property fact.

dealSpotter.headlineNumber: Separate observed condition from repair scope
dealSpotter.body: Ask the appropriate licensed professionals to define the work, timing, permits, access, exclusions, and uncertainty. Reconcile comparable written estimates, then update the model. The inspection alone does not establish the repair price or the correct contract response.

dealSpotter.address: Educational scenario: environmental or moisture finding
dealSpotter.headlineNumber: Confirm testing, source, and remediation requirements
dealSpotter.body: Follow the inspector's referral guidance and applicable local requirements. A mitigation method and cost depend on testing, building conditions, contractor scope, and jurisdiction. Review contract rights and deadlines with the relevant professionals.

Do not price or dismiss a structural concern from a photo or generic range. Obtain the appropriate engineering and contractor input, review financing and insurance implications, and keep unresolved scope visible in the acquisition model.

blogFeature.title: Property management yes or no — questions for the actual agreement
blogFeature.excerpt: If a manager will coordinate work, compare the quoted scope, approval authority, markup, vendor policy, records, and responsibility in the actual management agreement.

qa.question: Which inspection findings deserve follow-up?
qa.answer: Prioritize safety, active water or moisture, structure, roof and envelope, electrical, plumbing and sewer, HVAC, environmental conditions, and any issue the inspector refers to a specialist. Also review permits, code, insurance, financing, and tenant implications. The right follow-up and price are property- and jurisdiction-specific; obtain qualified local assessments and written estimates before relying on revised model assumptions.

shipNote.title: Update only reviewed assumptions
items: Free: revise the price and released operating assumptions, then rerun the preliminary screen
Keep inspection scope and contractor or specialist estimates outside the model as supporting evidence
An updated result is not an instruction to proceed, renegotiate, or terminate
